{"parentUuid":"230f7a88-25ad-4ee9-915d-4968e396e4db","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a62f3d0be4fa068fc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017xF8tXNnhKE8ms59vu57v4","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Prohibited patterns in manuscript prose\n2\t\n3\t**Shared reference. Read on drafting, and read again on review.** The `paper-authoring`\n4\tskill and the `prose-reviewer` agent both consume this file, so a rule cannot mean one\n5\tthing while writing and another while reviewing.\n6\t\n7\t⚠️ **This is the shared FLOOR, not the whole review.** The reviewer additionally carries\n8\treader-outcome questions that do not appear here and that an author must never be given as\n9\ta checklist: a generator optimises against any list it can see. See the skill's §\"Why the\n10\treviewer knows things this file does not\".\n11\t\n12\tEvery rule below was derived from a measured sweep of the 21-bundle corpus, not from a\n13\tstyle guide. Where a number appears, it is what was counted.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## 1. The em-dash: prohibited outright, including in headings\n18\t\n19\t**Never write `---` or a literal `—`.** Two forms exist and both are banned.\n20\t\n21\t**Why this one is absolute.** An em-dash reads as machine-authored to a 2026 reader and\n22\tcosts trust before the physics is evaluated. One is as disqualifying as forty, so there is\n23\tno acceptable density. Enforced by `validate.py --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free`, target\n24\tzero. Measured before the corpus was swept: **741 of them, and 0 of 21 bundles clean.**\n25\t\n26\t### ⚠️ The en-dash `--` is MANDATORY and must never be touched\n27\t\n28\t`--` (exactly two hyphens) is a different character doing a different job, and the corpus\n29\tcarries **1,121** of them:\n30\t\n31\t- compound eponyms: `Bose--Einstein`, `Bekenstein--Hawking`, `Schwinger--Keldysh`,\n32\t  `Kaul--Majumdar`, `Chowdhury--Hartnoll--Hebbar--Khondaker`, `SK--EFT`\n33\t- numeric ranges: `pp. 10--15`, `$2$--$3$ K`\n34\t\n35\t**An author over-correcting to \"no dashes at all\" breaks every compound name in the\n36\tprogram, and the check cannot see it** because it counts exactly three hyphens. This is the\n37\tsingle highest-cost mistake available here. One live line contained both:\n38\t`observables---also drives the SK--EFT`.\n39\t\n40\tA third variant exists in the wild: the literal Unicode en-dash `–` (U+2013), found as\n41\t`Kaul–Majumdar` and `Chowdhury–Hartnoll–Hebbar–Khondaker`. Write `--` instead; D3 once\n42\tspelled the same name both ways.\n43\t\n44\t### Replacing an em-dash is a REWRITE, not a substitution\n45\t\n46\tA mechanical swap produces comma splices. Identify the job the dash was doing, then use the\n47\tpunctuation that already exists for that job. Frequencies below are from six independent\n48\treadings of all 741 occurrences.\n49\t\n50\t| The dash was doing | Frequency | Write instead |\n51\t|---|---|---|\n52\t| Paired aside interrupting a clause | ~45–55% | parentheses; a comma pair when the aside is short and contains no commas of its own |\n53\t| Introducing an explanation, expansion or list | ~30–45% | a colon |\n54\t| Separating a label from its gloss in `\\item`, `\\subsection{}`, `\\paragraph{}` | ~15% | a colon, always |\n55\t| Contrastive \"X, not Y\" interjection | ~7% | a comma pair (parentheses would demote a correction to an aside) |\n56\t| Joining two independent clauses | ~3–15% | a semicolon, or a full stop and a new sentence |\n57\t| Trailing appositive glossing a number's significance | common in E1/E2 | a comma |\n58\t\n59\t### The four hard cases, each of which defeats a mechanical fix\n60\t\n61\t1. **The aside contains its own parenthetical or citation.** Converting the outer dash to\n62\t   parentheses yields stacked or nested parens that read as a stutter:\n63\t   `(\\lean{diamondDist_eq_choiSDP}) (the Watrous semidefinite program~\\cite{Watrous2018}) is proven`.\n64\t   **Merge the tag and the aside into ONE parenthetical** with an internal comma or\n65\t   semicolon. Do not nest.\n66\t2. **The aside contains a comma-separated list.** Comma-punctuating it makes the reader\n67\t   parse the inner items as continuing the outer sentence's list. Use parentheses.\n68\t3. **The sentence already has a colon later on.** Adding a second colon reads as a nested\n69\t   label. Restructure with a copula: `X is the headline theorem: Y`.\n70\t4. **Three levels of subordination.** An aside inside an aside inside a main clause is a\n71\t   sentence trying to be three sentences. Split it.\n72\t\n73\t### The generative habits behind them: prohibit these, not just the symbol\n74\t\n75\tAll six readers converged on the same root, so treat it as the rule that matters:\n76\t\n77\t> **Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification.** Write the clarification as\n78\t> its own sentence, before or after.\n79\t\n80\tThe dominant shape was *claim, dash, restatement-with-a-twist, dash, continuation*: draft a\n81\tclean declarative, then, worried a reader will misattribute a convention or miss a caveat,\n82\tsplice the qualifier into the middle. It concentrated in exactly the paragraphs doing the\n83\theaviest epistemic hedging (novelty disclaimers, provenance caveats, convention-pinning),\n84\twhich is where this project's prose is densest.\n85\t\n86\tFour more shapes, each of which reliably produces an em-dash:\n87\t\n88\t- **Name-then-gloss in itemised lists.** `\\item \\verb|foo_bar|: the substantive witness`.\n89\t  Use the colon from the start; this was the single most common pattern in the Lean-heavy\n90\t  bundles.\n91\t- **Label-then-gloss in headings.** `\\subsection{Pillar 1: Golterman--Shamir}`. A dash in a\n92\t  heading also reads as a tic when scanning the table of contents.\n93\t- **Tag-stacking.** A claim ending in a `\\lean{...}` identifier in parens, then a dash\n94\t  glossing that identifier. This is an appositive that got dash-punctuated only because the\n95\t  sentence had already spent its parentheses.\n96\t- **Claim-then-immediately-re-scope.** `T_H \\approx 2.4$ K --- nine orders of magnitude\n97\t  above atomic BEC --- with adiabaticity...`. A defensible instinct for a rigorous program,\n98\t  executed with the wrong punctuation: pick the syntax that matches the qualifier's\n99\t  grammatical role.\n100\t\n101\t---\n102\t\n103\t## 2. A fix may not narrate itself\n104\t\n105\t**Never tell the reader what an earlier draft of this paper said, when it was corrected, or\n106\twhich review round caught it.** A referee has no access to that process and cannot act on\n107\tit; the text reads as a changelog pasted into a manuscript.\n108\t\n109\tEnforced by `validate.py --check bundle_reader_facing_voice`, target zero. Banned forms:\n110\t\n111\t- a correction stamped with a date: `(corrected 2026-08-01)`\n112\t- an account of an earlier draft: `three earlier drafts of this paragraph asserted...`\n113\t- a first-person superseded claim: `We previously shipped a theorem asserting...`\n114\t- an internal review reference: `(D11 Stage-13 round-14 finding 6.2)`\n115\t- the project's own planning documents: `Our earlier planning documents described...`\n116\t- review rounds cast as actors: `rounds 7 and 10 both rated this cosmetic`\n117\t- a claim about the paper's own drafting: `typeset unconditionally in every draft`\n118\t\n119\t**The history is not lost, it moves.** `papers/<X>/change_log.md` and\n120\t`docs/review_finding_supersessions.json` are where a later reader can actually check it, and\n121\tthe ledger entry is required by the lift procedure anyway.\n122\t\n123\t### ⚠️ Removing narration is not deleting content\n124\t\n125\tMost of these passages wrap something real, and the substance must survive:\n126\t\n127\t- **A retraction is a scientific disclosure.** Restate it as a present-tense negative\n128\t  result: what is *not* claimed and why it fails. Do not delete the paragraph.\n129\t- **A scope correction states the correct scope.** Keep every factual statement about what\n130\t  a module does and does not contain, including file:line references. Drop only \"earlier\n131\t  drafts called it X\" and the date/round/finding tag.\n132\t- **A completeness disclaimer is a real caveat.** Keep it; drop the account of what two\n133\t  earlier drafts asserted.\n134\t\n135\t### What is NOT prohibited\n136\t\n137\tReporting that *the literature* corrected something is ordinary scholarship: `Smith\n138\tcorrected this coefficient in 2019` is correct and stays.\n139\t\n140\tDescribing the verification pipeline is legitimate **when the pipeline is the paper's\n141\tsubject matter** (I1, and I2/I3 for library conventions). Addressing the paper's own\n142\treferees is legitimate anywhere: `lets Mathlib4 reviewers calibrate expectations`.\n143\t\n144\tThis distinction is why the rule targets the *act* of self-narration rather than a\n145\tvocabulary. A word list banning `Stage 13`, `reviewer` and `adversarial review` scores 90\n146\thits on this corpus, of which 48 are legitimate uses in the methodology paper alone.\n147\t\n148\t---\n149\t\n150\t## 3. Claim discipline\n151\t\n152\tThese are enforced elsewhere in the pipeline; they are repeated here because they are\n153\tcheaper to satisfy while drafting than to repair at review.\n154\t\n155\t- **Never hedge a count or numerical literal with \"alt convention\" or \"+N depending on\n156\t  convention\" without proving the convention sensitivity.** If counts disagree across\n157\t  tools, find the truth. Convention-drift framing masks actual content drift: a \"161 ± 3\n158\t  alt convention\" was really 164, and the +3 was real drift.\n159\t- **Verify which registry a name lives in before citing it.** `AXIOM_METADATA`,\n160\t  `PLACEHOLDER_THEOREMS`, `HYPOTHESIS_REGISTRY` and `BORDISM_HYPOTHESES` are four different\n161\t  tables; a name found in one and attributed to another is a Stage-13 blocker.\n162\t- **Every cross-language prior-art claim must resolve to a verifiable URL or canonical\n163\t  ecosystem reference.** Hallucinated libraries have shipped before. When in doubt, cite\n164\t  the ecosystem (UniMath, Mathlib4) rather than naming a specific library.\n165\t- **When broadening an attribution, verify every addition belongs in the broadened\n166\t  category.** Surface code is abelian-stabiliser QEC, not non-Abelian-anyon TQC.\n167\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline.** Use `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n168\t  macros rather than typing a literal.\n169\t\n170\t---\n171\t\n172\t## 4. Structure\n173\t\n174\t- **The abstract leads with the result**, not with the programme, the architecture, or what\n175\t  the paper will do.\n176\t- **The reader never sees the project's internal taxonomy.** Not `bundle`, `tier`, `wave`,\n177\t  `phase`, or `splash`. Companion papers are cited as papers, by title, in a normal\n178\t  reference list. This is what makes a manuscript read as a repository index: F's organising\n179\t  vocabulary was its own publication plan.\n180\t- **Section architecture is authored, not accumulated.** A bundle's sections come from its\n181\t  charter, written before any source is registered. Do not add a section because a source\n182\t  was registered: D3 has 37 sections against 31 sources, which is sedimentation.\n183\t- **Every figure is planned.** A bundle with no figures is a charter defect, not a style\n184\t  choice; 9 of 21 bundles shipped zero figures because the lift step only ever *migrated*\n185\t  figures that already existed.\n186\t"}]},"uuid":"d6bd2901-4116-4b12-95ca-9f887b5fcaca","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:39:01.493Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"230f7a88-25ad-4ee9-915d-4968e396e4db","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

{"parentUuid":"0a8c16ad-ac41-47e4-9563-f9cb9d3d3f34","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a62f3d0be4fa068fc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GJp3TLQZcGQzR5xSTugTdn","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tname: paper-authoring\n3\tdescription: This skill should be used when the user asks to \"draft a paper section\", \"write the bundle draft\", \"author the manuscript\", \"lift content into a bundle\", \"write up this wave for publication\", \"draft the abstract\", \"revise the paper prose\", or when editing any `papers/<bundle>/paper_draft.tex`. Provides the house voice, the prohibited-pattern floor, and venue conventions for SK-EFT Hawking publication bundles.\n4\t---\n5\t\n6\t# Authoring a publication bundle\n7\t\n8\tGuidance for writing manuscript prose in `papers/<bundle>/paper_draft.tex`. This is the\n9\tgenerative counterpart to the `prose-reviewer` agent; both read the same prohibited-pattern\n10\treference so a rule cannot drift between writing and review.\n11\t\n12\tRead it either way you draft: the lead writing in-context, or a `paper-drafter` agent\n13\tdispatched over one section. `paper-drafter` reads this file and the same reference by\n14\tpath, so the floor is identical however the prose is produced.\n15\t\n16\t**Read `references/prohibited-patterns.md` before drafting.** It is mandatory, not\n17\tbackground, and it is short.\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Why this skill exists\n22\t\n23\tThe pipeline had three reviewer agents and no authoring guidance. Everything about how to\n24\twrite lived in `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` §7 as a bookkeeping checklist consulted at\n25\tlift time. The measured result of that gap, across 21 bundles:\n26\t\n27\t- **741 em-dashes**, with zero bundles clean\n28\t- **13 passages** narrating the paper's own correction history to a referee\n29\t- **9 of 21 bundles shipping zero figures**, because the lift step only migrated figures\n30\t  that already existed and no step ever planned one\n31\t- **D3 carrying 37 sections against 31 contributing sources**, which is sedimentation\n32\t  rather than architecture\n33\t\n34\tNone of that is a capability limit. It is what an unguided generator produces when the only\n35\tcontrols are downstream reviewers.\n36\t\n37\t---\n38\t\n39\t## Before writing a section\n40\t\n41\t1. **Read the charter.** `papers/<X>/bundle_metadata.json` carries `target_journal` and\n42\t   `length_target`; the section belongs to a planned outline, not to a source paper that\n43\t   happened to be registered.\n44\t2. **Read the substrate directly.** Contributing per-paper drafts, the Lean modules, the\n45\t   roadmap. Do not write from a summary.\n46\t3. **Know the claim this section makes** and which apex theorem backs it. A section whose\n47\t   claim has no Lean witness is a finding waiting to happen.\n48\t\n49\t## While writing\n50\t\n51\tWrite for a referee at the named venue who has never seen the repository, cannot run the\n52\tcode, and will not read a second sentence to understand the first.\n53\t\n54\t- **State the result, then support it.** Not the programme, not the architecture, not what\n55\t  the section will do.\n56\t- **One clause, one job.** Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification; write\n57\t  the clarification as its own sentence. This single habit produced most of the corpus's\n58\t  em-dashes.\n59\t- **No em-dash, ever** (`---` or `—`). **`--` is mandatory** for compound eponyms and\n60\t  ranges and must never be touched. Both rules and every replacement case are in\n61\t  `references/prohibited-patterns.md` §1; read them before reaching for a dash.\n62\t- **A fix never narrates itself.** Correct silently in the manuscript and record the history\n63\t  in `change_log.md` and the supersession ledger (§2 of the reference).\n64\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline** via `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n65\t  macros, never typed as literals.\n66\t- **Cite companion work as papers**, by title. The reader never sees `bundle`, `tier`,\n67\t  `wave`, `phase` or `splash`.\n68\t\n69\t## Before handing off\n70\t\n71\t```bash\n72\tuv run python scripts/compile_bundle_pdf.py <X>   # must be clean\n73\tuv run python scripts/validate.py \\\n74\t    --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free \\\n75\t    --check bundle_reader_facing_voice \\\n76\t    --check bundle_manuscript_length\n77\t```\n78\t\n79\tCompile through `compile_bundle_pdf.py`, never `pdflatex` inside `papers/<X>/`. An in-place\n80\tcompile clobbers `paper_draft.{aux,log,synctex.gz}`, and a reviewer running concurrently then\n81\tjudges your draft by a `.log` that belongs to someone else's pass.\n82\t\n83\tAll three are deterministic and all three must pass. They are a floor, not a review: they\n84\tconfirm nothing prohibited is present, and say nothing about whether the argument carries.\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## Why the reviewer knows things this file does not\n89\t\n90\tThe `prose-reviewer` agent reads this same reference, so the two never disagree about a\n91\trule. It also carries a brief that is deliberately **not** written down here, framed on\n92\treader outcome rather than rule compliance: where a reader would stop, whether the abstract\n93\tleads with the result, whether each section advances a single argument.\n94\t\n95\tThat asymmetry is intentional. A generator optimises against any checklist it can see, so a\n96\treviewer briefed entirely off the author's rules would pass anything the author produced.\n97\tSatisfying this file is necessary and not sufficient.\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t\n101\t## Additional resources\n102\t\n103\t### Reference files\n104\t\n105\t- **`references/prohibited-patterns.md`** — mandatory read. The em-dash prohibition and its\n106\t  replacement cases, the self-narration ban, claim discipline, structure rules. Shared with\n107\t  the `prose-reviewer` agent.\n108\t\n109\t### Related surfaces\n110\t\n111\t- `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` — the 14-step lift workflow this drafting sits inside\n112\t  (§7 authoring, §11 the BLOCKER loop, §12a the terminal de-scarring pass).\n113\t- `docs/WAVE_EXECUTION_PIPELINE.md` Stage 10 — the process law and its gates.\n114\t- `docs/BUNDLE_DIRECTORY_SCHEMA.md` — `length_target`, `apex_theorems`, and who writes what.\n115\t"}]},"uuid":"29b6b4d9-f657-46fa-b410-ac77ebd5ac79","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:39:11.731Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0a8c16ad-ac41-47e4-9563-f9cb9d3d3f34","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

This is the Wave 5 expression of Decision Gate E.2\n306\t— the Wave 1 closure\n307\t`a2_matches_GNemerg_iff_alpha_ADW_unity` re-stated at the\n308\tmicroscopic-coefficient level.\n309\t\n310\tSubstantive: forward direction uses positivity of `G_N_from_a2`\n311\t(`G_N_from_a2_pos`, Wave 1) to flip `mul_eq_zero`; reverse is\n312\tdef-substitution. -/\n313\ttheorem matchResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity\n314\t    {Λ_UV N_f α_ADW : ℝ} (hΛ : 0 < Λ_UV) (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n315\t    matchResidual Λ_UV N_f α_ADW = 0 ↔ α_ADW = 1 := by\n316\t  rw [matchResidual_eq_alpha_minus_one_times_GN]\n317\t  have hG_pos : 0 < G_N_from_a2 Λ_UV N_f := G_N_from_a2_pos hΛ hN\n318\t  have hG_ne : G_N_from_a2 Λ_UV N_f ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hG_pos\n319\t  constructor\n320\t  · intro h\n321\t    have h_alpha_minus_one : α_ADW - 1 = 0 :=\n322\t      (mul_eq_zero.mp h).resolve_right hG_ne\n323\t    linarith\n324\t  · intro h\n325\t    rw [h]; ring\n326\t\n327\t/-! ## §4. Cross-bridges to Phase 6a.1, Wave 1, and Wave 2 -/\n328\t\n329\t/-- **Substantive cross-bridge (Phase 6a.1 + Wave 1).**  At the\n330\tSakharov-Adler calibration `α_ADW = 1`, the microscopic Newton\n331\tconstant equals the Phase 6a.1 emergent Newton constant.  Proof body\n332\tinvokes both `LinearizedEFE.G_N_emerg_at_alpha_one` and\n333\t`HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2_eq_G_N_sakharov` by name —\n334\tdrift-protection per `feedback_python_lean_refs_drift.md` (P6\n335\tcross-module bridge integrity). -/\n336\ttheorem gNMicroscopic_at_alpha_one_eq_G_N_emerg\n337\t    (Λ_UV N_f : ℝ) :\n338\t    gNMicroscopic Λ_UV N_f 1 =\n339\t      SKEFTHawking.LinearizedEFE.G_N_emerg Λ_UV N_f 1 := by\n340\t  unfold gNMicroscopic\n341\t  rw [SKEFTHawking.LinearizedEFE.G_N_emerg_at_alpha_one Λ_UV N_f]\n342\t  rw [← SKEFTHawking.HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2_eq_G_N_sakharov Λ_UV N_f]\n343\t  ring\n344\t\n345\t/-- **Stelle-basis sum closed form.**  The aggregate `α + β + γ` of\n346\tthe Wave 2 Stelle coefficients evaluates in closed form to\n347\t`-(7 N_f / 810) · (4π)⁻²`.  Substantive cross-bridge: combines the\n348\tthree Wave 2 definitions `a4_alpha`, `a4_beta`, `a4_gamma` into a\n349\tsingle rational aggregate, exposing a *different* numerical\n350\tfingerprint than any individual coefficient (the rationals\n351\t`-1/324, -41/4320, +17/4320` combine to `-7/810` — non-trivial\n352\trational arithmetic). -/\n353\ttheorem higherCurvature_stelle_sum_eq (N_f : ℝ) :\n354\t    a4_alpha N_f + a4_beta N_f + a4_gamma N_f =\n355\t      -(7 * N_f / 810) * fourPiSqInv := by\n356\t  unfold a4_alpha a4_beta a4_gamma\n357\t  ring\n358\t\n359\t/-- **Stelle-basis sum sign aggregate.**  For positive species count,\n360\tthe sum `α + β + γ` is strictly negative.  Substantive composite:\n361\tthis is *not* implied by any individual `a4_*` sign theorem\n362\t(`a4_alpha_neg` covers only `α`, etc.); the aggregate sign is its own\n363\tload-bearing structural fact, used by the bundle witness. -/\n364\ttheorem higherCurvature_stelle_sum_negative\n365\t    {N_f : ℝ} (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n366\t    a4_alpha N_f + a4_beta N_f + a4_gamma N_f < 0 := by\n367\t  rw [higherCurvature_stelle_sum_eq]\n368\t  have h_inv_pos : 0 < fourPiSqInv := fourPiSqInv_pos\n369\t  nlinarith\n370\t\n371\t/-! ## §5. Tracked-Prop bundle for microscopic-macroscopic match -/\n372\t\n373\t/-- **Bundled predicate for the microscopic-macroscopic match.**  An\n374\t`(Λ_UV, N_f, α_ADW)` triple \"matches at the microscopic-coefficient\n375\tlevel\" iff:\n376\t\n377\t  1. The match residual `δG := gNMicroscopic − G_N_from_a2` vanishes\n378\t     (Wave 5 §3 Decision-Gate biconditional content);\n379\t  2. The Wave 2 Stelle-basis sum `α + β + γ` is strictly negative\n382\t     (Wave 5 §4 — composite sign signature inherited from Wave 2).\n383\t\n384\tEach conjunct invokes a *distinct* Wave (5 / 5 / 2) substantive\n385\ttheorem with distinct algebraic content; not P2 redundancy.  Each\n386\tconjunct genuinely separates \"Wave 5 microscopic-macroscopic match\n387\tat the calibrated point\" from any of the three failure modes\n388\t(off-calibration `α_ADW`, vanishing `Λ^emerg`, or sign-flip in the\n389\thigher-curvature aggregate). -/\n390\tdef H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch\n391\t    (Λ_UV N_f α_ADW : ℝ) : Prop :=\n392\t  matchResidual Λ_UV N_f α_ADW = 0 ∧\n393\t  0 < lambdaEmergMicroscopic Λ_UV N_f ∧\n394\t  a4_alpha N_f + a4_beta N_f + a4_gamma N_f < 0\n395\t\n396\t/-- **Dirac witness at the Sakharov-Adler calibration.**  Under\n397\tpositive `(Λ_UV, N_f)` and the calibration value `α_ADW = 1`, the\n398\tmicroscopic-macroscopic match bundle holds.\n399\t\n400\tSubstantive cross-bridges: each conjunct invokes a *distinct*\n401\tsubstantive theorem by name — `matchResidual_at_alpha_one` (Wave 5\n402\t§3), `lambdaEmergMicroscopic_pos` (Wave 5 §2), and\n403\t`higherCurvature_stelle_sum_negative` (Wave 5 §4 / Wave 2).  Not P2\n404\tredundancy. -/\n405\ttheorem dirac_H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch_at_alpha_one\n406\t    {Λ_UV N_f : ℝ} (hΛ : 0 < Λ_UV) (hN : 0 < N_f) :\n407\t    H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch Λ_UV N_f 1 := by\n408\t  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩\n409\t  · exact matchResidual_at_alpha_one Λ_UV N_f\n410\t  · exact lambdaEmergMicroscopic_pos hΛ hN\n411\t  · exact higherCurvature_stelle_sum_negative hN\n412\t\n413\t/-- **Falsifier-witness for non-calibrated `α_ADW`.**  Under positive\n414\t`(Λ_UV, N_f)` and *any* `α_ADW ≠ 1`, the microscopic-macroscopic\n415\tmatch fails — specifically its first conjunct (the match residual).\n416\t\n417\tSubstantive scope: rules out the trivial reading \"any `α_ADW`\n418\tsatisfies the bundle\"; the predicate genuinely singles out the\n419\tSakharov-Adler calibration.  Drift-protection: proof body invokes\n420\t`matchResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity` (Wave 5 §3) by name. -/\n421\ttheorem perturbed_alpha_not_H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch\n422\t    {Λ_UV N_f α_ADW : ℝ}\n423\t    (hΛ : 0 < Λ_UV) (hN : 0 < N_f) (hα : α_ADW ≠ 1) :\n424\t    ¬ H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch Λ_UV N_f α_ADW := by\n425\t  intro ⟨h_match, _, _⟩\n426\t  have h_eq := (matchResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity hΛ hN).mp h_match\n427\t  exact hα h_eq\n428\t\n429\tend SKEFTHawking.MicroscopicCoefficientMatch\n430\t\n431\tend\n432\t"}]},"uuid":"69c447ba-90a2-4ca8-8510-82191f1d1de8","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:39:15.399Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f6c86eea-3f5a-4d63-b88d-432079a210e4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

{"parentUuid":"14fd8897-1697-4939-9f00-0203bbb14f6d","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a62f3d0be4fa068fc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PqJsTF2rmGkGPVFMLB6r1N","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport Mathlib\n2\timport SKEFTHawking.Basic\n3\timport SKEFTHawking.HeatKernelExpansion\n4\timport SKEFTHawking.HigherCurvatureStructure\n5\t\n6\t/-!\n7\t# Phase 6e Wave 3: Nonlinear Diffeomorphism Invariance (Path-b)\n8\t\n9\t## Goal\n10\t\n11\tPath-(b) direct check that the Seeley-DeWitt heat-kernel effective\n12\tLagrangian is **diffeomorphism-invariant order-by-order** in the\n13\tasymptotic expansion (orders `a_0, a_2, a_4`).\n14\t\n15\tFor a scalar density `L` built from polynomial scalar curvature\n16\tinvariants `{1, R, R², R_μν R^μν, R_μνρσ R^μνρσ}` (equivalently,\n17\tStelle's `{1, R, R², C², 𝒢}`), the variation of `√g · L` under an\n18\tinfinitesimal coordinate transformation `x^μ → x^μ + ξ^μ` is a total\n19\tdivergence\n20\t\n21\t  `δ_ξ (√g L) = ∂_μ(ξ^μ √g L)`,\n22\t\n23\tso the action `∫ √g L` is diff-invariant on a closed manifold.  The\n24\t**path-b \"anomaly residual\"** at order `n` is the algebraic mismatch\n25\tbetween the same density expressed in two equivalent scalar-invariant\n26\tbases:\n27\t\n28\t  `residual_n(L; B₁, B₂) := L_density_in_B₁ − L_density_in_B₂`.\n29\t\n30\tFor the Wave 1 Christensen-Duff Dirac coefficient bundle this residual\n31\tvanishes identically at orders 0, 2, and 4 — the order-4 case is\n32\texactly the Wave 2 main theorem\n33\t`a4_density_eq_a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis`.\n34\t\n35\t## Module structure\n36\t\n37\t- §1: `EffectiveLagrangianCoefs` (5-coefficient bundle through a_4)\n38\t  + `density` evaluator\n39\t- §2: `diracCoefBundle` — canonical Wave 1 Christensen-Duff Dirac\n40\t  bundle for `N_f` species\n41\t- §3: `DiffInvariantAt` predicate + `pathB_residual_at_order` order\n42\t  index → residual evaluator\n43\t- §4: Order-`a_4` zero-residual theorem (orders 0/2 are definitionally\n44\t  zero; their content is consumed inline at §5)\n45\t- §5: Order-by-order `DiffInvariantAt`-witnesses for the Dirac bundle\n46\t- §6: **CORRECTNESS-PUSH** biconditional: order-by-order diff-invariance\n47\t  ⇔ basis-change consistency at order 4 (Wave 2 main identity)\n48\t- §7: Falsifier — non-admissible bundle has nonzero residual\n49\t- §8: Tracked-Prop `H_NonlinearDiffInvariance` + Dirac witness\n50\t\n51\t## References\n52\t\n53\t- Wald, *General Relativity*, App. E.1 — diff invariance via Lie\n54\t  derivatives + total divergences\n55\t- Vassilevich, Phys. Rep. 388, 279 (2003), §3.1 — covariance of\n56\t  heat-kernel coefficients under coordinate transformations\n57\t- Phase 6e Wave 1 `HeatKernelExpansion.lean` — Christensen-Duff Dirac\n58\t  coefficient bundle (input)\n59\t- Phase 6e Wave 2 `HigherCurvatureStructure.lean` — Stelle basis\n60\t  change at order `a_4` (path-b consistency at the basis level)\n61\t\n62\t## Scope lock\n63\t\n64\tIN SCOPE: algebraic path-b residual at orders 0, 2, 4 expressed at the\n65\tcoefficient-bundle level; consistency of the Wave 2 basis change as\n66\tthe load-bearing diff-invariance content at a_4; structural falsifier\n67\tfor non-admissible (non-scalar-invariant) bundles.\n68\t\n69\tOUT OF SCOPE: PDE-level proof of the full `δ_ξ(√g L) = ∂_μ(...)` identity\n70\ton a manifold (deferred to Mathlib's diff-geom infrastructure when\n71\tready); higher orders `a_6, …` (deferred — out of scope for the\n72\tmean-field 6e program per strategy doc §15); path-(a) symmetry-\n73\tenhancement emergence (backlog per roadmap O.3).\n74\t-/\n75\t\n76\tnoncomputable section\n77\t\n78\topen Real\n79\t\n80\tnamespace SKEFTHawking.NonlinearDiffInvariance\n81\t\n82\topen SKEFTHawking.HeatKernelExpansion\n83\topen SKEFTHawking.HigherCurvatureStructure\n84\t\n85\t/-! ## §1. Effective Lagrangian coefficient bundle -/\n86\t\n87\t/-- Coefficient bundle for the Seeley-DeWitt effective Lagrangian\n88\tthrough order `a_4`.  Five coefficients:\n89\t\n90\t  - `a0` — constant scalar piece (cosmological-constant-scale density)\n91\t  - `a2_R` — coefficient of the Ricci scalar `R`\n92\t  - `a4_R_sq` — coefficient of `R²`\n93\t  - `a4_Ricci_sq` — coefficient of `R_μν R^μν`\n94\t  - `a4_Riemann_sq` — coefficient of `R_μνρσ R^μνρσ`\n95\t\n96\tThis is the \"natural\" `{1, R, R², R_μν², R_μνρσ²}` basis; the Stelle\n97\t`{R², C², 𝒢}` reduction at order 4 is provided through the basis-change\n98\tof Wave 2. -/\n99\tstructure EffectiveLagrangianCoefs where\n100\t  a0 : ℝ\n101\t  a2_R : ℝ\n102\t  a4_R_sq : ℝ\n103\t  a4_Ricci_sq : ℝ\n104\t  a4_Riemann_sq : ℝ\n105\t\n106\t/-- Evaluate the order-by-order density of an effective Lagrangian\n107\tbundle at given curvature-invariant data\n108\t`(R, R_sq, Ricci_sq, Riemann_sq)`.\n109\t\n110\t  `density L (R, R², R_μν², R_μνρσ²) :=`\n111\t    `L.a0 + L.a2_R · R + L.a4_R_sq · R² + L.a4_Ricci_sq · R_μν²`\n112\t    `       + L.a4_Riemann_sq · R_μνρσ²`. -/\n113\tdef EffectiveLagrangianCoefs.density\n114\t    (L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs)\n115\t    (R R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n116\t  L.a0 + L.a2_R * R\n117\t       + L.a4_R_sq * R_sq\n118\t       + L.a4_Ricci_sq * Ricci_sq\n119\t       + L.a4_Riemann_sq * Riemann_sq\n120\t\n121\t/-- Density of an effective Lagrangian bundle at order `a_4` only —\n122\tthe higher-curvature piece without `a_0` or `a_2 R` contributions.\n123\tThis is the part affected by the Wave 2 Stelle basis change. -/\n124\tdef EffectiveLagrangianCoefs.density_a4\n125\t    (L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs)\n126\t    (R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n127\t  L.a4_R_sq * R_sq\n128\t    + L.a4_Ricci_sq * Ricci_sq\n129\t    + L.a4_Riemann_sq * Riemann_sq\n130\t\n131\t/-! ## §2. Wave 1 canonical Dirac coefficient bundle -/\n132\t\n133\t/-- Canonical Christensen-Duff Dirac effective-Lagrangian bundle for\n134\t`N_f` fermion species, as derived in Wave 1 (`HeatKernelExpansion`).\n135\tFive coefficients pinned by Wave 1 closed forms; this is the bundle\n136\twhose diff invariance the rest of the module establishes.\n137\t\n138\tSubstantive cross-bridge: every coefficient is a *named call* into\n139\tWave 1 (`a0_dirac`, `a2_R_coefficient`, `a4_R_sq_coef`, etc.) — drift-\n140\tprotection per `feedback_python_lean_refs_drift.md` (P6 cross-module\n141\tbridge integrity). -/\n142\tdef diracCoefBundle (N_f : ℝ) : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs where\n143\t  a0            := a0_dirac N_f\n144\t  a2_R          := a2_R_coefficient N_f\n145\t  a4_R_sq       := a4_R_sq_coef N_f\n146\t  a4_Ricci_sq   := a4_Ricci_sq_coef N_f\n147\t  a4_Riemann_sq := a4_Riemann_sq_coef N_f\n148\t\n149\t/-- The order-`a_4` density of the Dirac bundle, written through Wave\n150\t1 named coefficients, equals the Wave 2 `a4_density` evaluator.\n151\tSubstantive bridge: ties the Wave 3 bundle abstraction to the Wave 2\n152\tbasis-change apparatus (proof unfolds both definitions, then `rfl`). -/\n153\ttheorem diracCoefBundle_density_a4_eq_wave2_a4_density\n154\t    (N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ) :\n155\t    (diracCoefBundle N_f).density_a4 R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq =\n156\t      a4_density N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq := by\n157\t  unfold EffectiveLagrangianCoefs.density_a4 diracCoefBundle a4_density\n158\t  rfl\n159\t\n160\t/-! ## §3. Path-b anomaly residual + DiffInvariantAt predicate -/\n161\t\n162\t/-- **Path-b anomaly residual at order `a_4`** for an effective\n163\tLagrangian bundle.  Defined as the algebraic difference between the\n164\torder-4 density expressed in the natural `{R², R_μν², R_μνρσ²}` basis\n165\tand the same density re-expressed in Stelle's `{R², C², 𝒢}` basis with\n166\tcoefficients `(α, β, γ)` derived from the `(c_R², c_Ricci², c_Riemann²)`\n167\tof the bundle via the Wave 2 3×3 linear-system solve.\n168\t\n169\tFor *bundles whose order-4 coefficients agree with Wave 1's Dirac\n170\ttable*, the basis change is consistent and the residual vanishes\n171\tidentically (Wave 2 main theorem).  For arbitrary bundles, the\n172\tresidual is a generic real number — the falsifier in §7 exhibits a\n173\tnonzero case. -/\n174\tdef pathB_residual_a4\n175\t    (L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs) (N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n176\t  L.density_a4 R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq -\n177\t    a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n178\t\n179\t/-- Path-b anomaly residual at order `a_2`: the structural piece\n180\t`L.a2_R · R` is a polynomial in the *single* scalar invariant `R`, so\n181\tno basis change is involved at this order — the residual is identically\n182\tzero by construction.  We define it as `0` for API uniformity with the\n183\torder-4 case. -/\n184\tdef pathB_residual_a2 (_L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs) (_R : ℝ) : ℝ := 0\n185\t\n186\t/-- Path-b anomaly residual at order `a_0`: a constant scalar has no\n187\tdiff variation, so the residual is identically zero. -/\n188\tdef pathB_residual_a0 (_L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs) : ℝ := 0\n189\t\n190\t/-- **Order-by-order diff-invariance predicate at the bundle level.**\n191\tA bundle `L` is *path-b diff-invariant at order `n` against species\n192\tcount `N_f`* iff its anomaly residual at order `n` (parameterized by\n193\tthe `N_f`-dependent Stelle basis change at order 4) vanishes for *all*\n194\tcurvature-invariant inputs.\n195\t\n196\tWe encode the three orders as a small case split:\n197\t\n198\t  - `n = 0`: `pathB_residual_a0` is identically zero\n199\t  - `n = 2`: for all `R`, `pathB_residual_a2 = 0`\n200\t  - `n = 4`: for all `(R_sq, Ricci_sq, Riemann_sq)`,\n201\t    `pathB_residual_a4 = 0`\n202\t\n203\tSubstantive content: at order 4, the predicate forces the bundle's\n204\torder-4 density to match the Stelle representation pointwise — exactly\n205\tthe diff-invariance content. -/\n206\tdef DiffInvariantAt\n207\t    (L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs) (N_f : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=\n208\t  if n = 0 then pathB_residual_a0 L = 0\n209\t  else if n = 2 then ∀ R : ℝ, pathB_residual_a2 L R = 0\n210\t  else if n = 4 then ∀ R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ,\n211\t    pathB_residual_a4 L N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq = 0\n212\t  else True  -- orders outside {0, 2, 4} are out-of-scope here\n213\t\n214\t/-! ## §4. Order-by-order zero-residual theorems\n215\t\n216\tThe order-0 and order-2 path-b residuals are *definitionally zero* —\n217\tencoded directly into `pathB_residual_a0` and `pathB_residual_a2` as\n218\tthe constant `0`.  No standalone theorems are needed at those orders;\n219\tthe `rfl` content is consumed inline by the §5 `DiffInvariantAt`\n220\twitnesses (`dirac_diffInvariantAt_zero/two`).\n221\t\n222\tThe substantive content of this section lives in the order-4 case,\n223\twhich consumes the Wave 2 main basis-change identity.\n224\t-/\n225\t\n226\t/-- **MAIN order-`a_4` zero-residual theorem for the Dirac bundle.**\n227\tFor the Christensen-Duff Wave 1 coefficient bundle and *all* curvature\n228\tinputs, the path-b basis-change anomaly vanishes:\n229\t\n230\t  `pathB_residual_a4 (diracCoefBundle N_f) N_f R² R_μν² R_μνρσ² = 0`.\n231\t\n232\t**Substantive cross-bridge to Wave 2:** the proof body invokes\n233\t`a4_density_eq_a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis` (Wave 2 main theorem) by\n234\tname, after rewriting the Dirac bundle's `density_a4` into Wave 2's\n235\t`a4_density` via `diracCoefBundle_density_a4_eq_wave2_a4_density`.\n236\t\n237\tThe biconditional in §6 (`diff_invariance_a4_iff_dirac_basis_consistent`)\n238\tshows this is the *load-bearing* substantive content of path-b diff\n239\tinvariance at a_4 — without the Wave 2 basis-change identity, this\n240\ttheorem would not hold.  P6 drift-protection per\n241\t`feedback_python_lean_refs_drift.md`. -/\n242\ttheorem pathB_residual_a4_dirac_eq_zero\n243\t    (N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ) :\n244\t    pathB_residual_a4 (diracCoefBundle N_f) N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq = 0 := by\n245\t  unfold pathB_residual_a4\n246\t  rw [diracCoefBundle_density_a4_eq_wave2_a4_density]\n247\t  -- Goal: a4_density - a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis = 0\n248\t  rw [a4_density_eq_a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis]\n249\t  ring\n250\t\n251\t/-! ## §5. Order-by-order `DiffInvariantAt` witnesses -/\n252\t\n253\t/-- Dirac bundle is diff-invariant at order `a_0`.  Discharge: at\n254\torder 0 the residual is definitionally `0` (constant scalar carries no\n255\tcurvature dependence). -/\n256\ttheorem dirac_diffInvariantAt_zero (N_f : ℝ) :\n257\t    DiffInvariantAt (diracCoefBundle N_f) N_f 0 := by\n258\t  unfold DiffInvariantAt pathB_residual_a0\n259\t  simp\n260\t\n261\t/-- Dirac bundle is diff-invariant at order `a_2`.  Discharge: at\n262\torder 2 the only invariant is `R` itself, no basis-change exists, and\n263\tthe residual is definitionally `0`. -/\n264\ttheorem dirac_diffInvariantAt_two (N_f : ℝ) :\n265\t    DiffInvariantAt (diracCoefBundle N_f) N_f 2 := by\n266\t  unfold DiffInvariantAt pathB_residual_a2\n267\t  intro _R; rfl\n268\t\n269\t/-- **Dirac bundle is diff-invariant at order `a_4`** — the load-bearing\n270\tWave 3 case.  Substantive cross-bridge: this is `dirac_diffInvariantAt_two`'s\n271\torder-4 sibling, and unlike orders 0 and 2 it consumes the Wave 2 main\n272\tidentity through `pathB_residual_a4_dirac_eq_zero`. -/\n273\ttheorem dirac_diffInvariantAt_four (N_f : ℝ) :\n274\t    DiffInvariantAt (diracCoefBundle N_f) N_f 4 := by\n275\t  unfold DiffInvariantAt\n276\t  intro R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n277\t  exact pathB_residual_a4_dirac_eq_zero N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n278\t\n279\t/-! ## §6. Correctness-push biconditional (general + Dirac-specialized) -/\n280\t\n281\t/-- **STRONGER bundle-generic biconditional.**  For *any* effective\n282\tLagrangian bundle `L` and any species count `N_f`, path-(b) diff\n283\tinvariance at order 4 is equivalent to the bundle's `density_a4` agreeing\n284\tpointwise with the Stelle-basis representation `a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis`:\n285\t\n286\t  `DiffInvariantAt L N_f 4`\n287\t    `↔ ∀ R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq,`\n288\t       `L.density_a4 R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq`\n289\t         `= a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq`.\n290\t\n291\tThis is bundle-independent: the substantive content of order-4 path-(b)\n292\tinvariance is *exactly* basis-change consistency for the bundle's\n293\t`density_a4`, regardless of which bundle is supplied.  The Dirac\n294\tspecialization (next theorem) composes this with Wave 2's\n295\t`a4_density_eq_a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis` to recover the original\n296\tformulation. -/\n297\ttheorem diff_invariance_a4_iff_basis_consistent\n298\t    (L : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs) (N_f : ℝ) :\n299\t    DiffInvariantAt L N_f 4 ↔\n300\t      ∀ R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ,\n301\t        L.density_a4 R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq =\n302\t          a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq := by\n303\t  unfold DiffInvariantAt\n304\t  simp only [if_neg (by decide : (4 : ℕ) ≠ 0),\n305\t              if_neg (by decide : (4 : ℕ) ≠ 2)]\n306\t  constructor\n307\t  · intro h R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n308\t    have := h R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n309\t    unfold pathB_residual_a4 at this\n310\t    linarith\n311\t  · intro h R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n312\t    unfold pathB_residual_a4\n313\t    rw [h]; Falsifier: non-admissible bundle has nonzero residual -/\n345\t\n346\t/-- A non-admissible \"perturbed\" bundle: the Dirac bundle with the\n347\torder-4 R² coefficient shifted by a nonzero scalar `δ`.  For nonzero\n348\t`δ`, this bundle does *not* satisfy the Wave 2 basis-change identity\n349\t(it differs from the Dirac bundle exactly by `δ` at the R²-channel).\n350\t-/\n351\tdef perturbedCoefBundle (N_f δ : ℝ) : EffectiveLagrangianCoefs where\n352\t  a0            := a0_dirac N_f\n353\t  a2_R          := a2_R_coefficient N_f\n354\t  a4_R_sq       := a4_R_sq_coef N_f + δ\n355\t  a4_Ricci_sq   := a4_Ricci_sq_coef N_f\n356\t  a4_Riemann_sq := a4_Riemann_sq_coef N_f\n357\t\n358\t/-- **STRONGER falsifier (general linearity).**  At *any* curvature\n359\tinput `(R_sq, Ricci_sq, Riemann_sq)`, the perturbed bundle's path-b\n360\t`a_4` residual equals exactly `δ * R_sq`.  Substantive: the perturbation\n361\tis in the `R²`-channel coefficient, so the residual response is linear\n362\tin `R_sq` (and zero when `R_sq = 0`, regardless of the other curvature\n363\tinputs) — exposing the *channel* of the falsifier.\n364\t\n365\tProof: rewrite `density_in_RC2GB_basis` via Wave 2's main identity to\n366\t`a4_density`, then unfold both `a4_density` instances; the only surviving\n367\tterm is the `R²`-channel difference `δ * R_sq`. Closes by `ring`.\n368\t\n369\tSubsumes the unit-`R²` corollary (`perturbed_pathB_residual_a4_at_unit_R_sq`)\n370\tand matches the Python test `test_residual_scales_with_R_sq_at_fixed_delta`. -/\n371\ttheorem perturbed_pathB_residual_a4_eq_delta_R_sq\n372\t    (N_f δ R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq : ℝ) :\n373\t    pathB_residual_a4 (perturbedCoefBundle N_f δ) N_f\n374\t        R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq = δ * R_sq := by\n375\t  unfold pathB_residual_a4 perturbedCoefBundle\n376\t       EffectiveLagrangianCoefs.density_a4\n377\t  rw [show a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq\n378\t        = a4_density N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq from\n379\t        (a4_density_eq_a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis\n380\t            N_f R_sq Ricci_sq Riemann_sq).symm]\n381\t  unfold a4_density\n382\t  ring\n383\t\n384\t/-- **Falsifier (unit-R² corollary).**  The perturbed bundle's path-b\n385\t`a_4` residual at `R_sq = 1, Ricci_sq = Riemann_sq = 0` equals the\n386\tperturbation `δ`. {N_f δ : ℝ} (hδ : (1 : ℝ) / 10 ^ (12 : ℕ) < |δ|) :\n433\t    (1 : ℝ) / 10 ^ (12 : ℕ) <\n434\t      |pathB_residual_a4 (perturbedCoefBundle N_f δ) N_f 1 0 0| := by\n435\t  rw Quantitative observational-bound theorems (correctness-push) -/\n277\t\n278\t/-- **Kostelecky bound is strictly tighter than Hughes-Drever.**\n279\tSubstantive numerical fact: `1/10³¹ < 1/10²⁹`, so any prediction\n280\tsatisfying the Kostelecky bound *automatically* satisfies the\n281\tHughes-Drever bound.  Used by the chained-bound theorem below.  Not\n282\ta P3 trivial-multiplication: the substantive content is the\n283\tstrict-ordering of the two published bounds. -/\n284\ttheorem torsionBoundKostelecky_lt_hughesDrever :\n285\t    torsionBoundKostelecky < torsionBoundHughesDrever := by\n286\t  unfold torsionBoundKostelecky torsionBoundHughesDrever\n287\t  -- 1/10^31 < 1/10^29 follows from 10^29 < 10^31.\n288\t  have h29 : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) := pow_pos (by norm_num) _\n289\t  have h31 : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) := pow_pos (by norm_num) _\n290\t  have h_lt : (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) := by\n291\t    have : (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) * 1 < (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) * 100 := by\n292\t      have h_pos : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) := h29\n293\t      nlinarith\n294\t    have h_eq : (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) = (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) * 100 := by\n295\t      have h_split : (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) = (10 : ℝ) ^ (29 : ℕ) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (2 : ℕ) := by\n296\t        rw [← pow_add]\n297\t      rw [h_split]; norm_num\n298\t    rw [h_eq]; linarith\n299\t  exact one_div_lt_one_div_of_lt h29 h_lt\n300\t\n301\t/-- **MAIN correctness-push: torsion at natural microscopic params is\n302\tquantitatively below the Kostelecky bound.**  At `(Λ_UV, N_f, α_EC) =\n303\t(planckMassGeV, 16, 1)` and the cosmological-bath spin density, the\n304\tpredicted torsion amplitude `|T_EC|` is strictly less than the\n305\tKostelecky-Russell-Tasson published bound `1/10³¹ GeV`.\n306\t\n307\tConcretely we prove `torsionAtCosmologicalBackground planckMassGeV\n308\t16 1 < torsionBoundKostelecky`.  The natural-parameter prediction is\n309\t`|T_EC| = 12π/(16 · planckMassGeV²) · 13/10⁴⁰ ≃ 2.05×10⁻⁷⁷ GeV`,\n310\twhich sits ~46 orders of magnitude below the bound.\n311\t\n312\t**Substantive Decision-Gate-style anchor:** quantitatively connects\n313\tthe Wave 6 microscopic prediction to the published observational\n314\tbound, making the \"torsion bound matched\" claim falsifiable in the\n315\tstrong sense (any future Wave-6-derived prediction with `|T_EC| ≥\n316\t10⁻³¹` would violate this theorem). -/\n317\ttheorem torsionAtCosmologicalBackground_at_planck_natural_below_kostelecky :\n318\t    torsionAtCosmologicalBackground planckMassGeV 16 1 <\n319\t      torsionBoundKostelecky := by\n320\t  unfold torsionAtCosmologicalBackground torsionAmplitude gNMicroscopic\n321\t        G_N_from_a2 cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3 planckMassGeV\n322\t        torsionBoundKostelecky\n323\t  -- Goal: 1 * (12π / (16 · (12·10^18)²)) * (13/10^40) < 1/10^31.\n324\t  have hpi_lt : Real.pi < 3.15 := Real.pi_lt_d2\n325\t  have hpi_pos : 0 < Real.pi := Real.pi_pos\n326\t  have h36 : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ) := pow_pos (by norm_num) _\n327\t  have h40 : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ) := pow_pos (by norm_num) _\n328\t  have h31 : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) := pow_pos (by norm_num) _\n329\t  have h_combine : (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ) = (10 : ℝ) ^ (76 : ℕ) := by\n330\t    rw [← pow_add]\n331\t  have h_split : (10 : ℝ) ^ (76 : ℕ) = (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ) := by\n332\t    rw [← pow_add]\n333\t  -- Step 1: collapse (12·10^18)^2 = 144·10^36.\n334\t  have h_sq_eq : (12 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (18 : ℕ)) ^ 2 = 144 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ) := by\n335\t    have h1 : (12 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (18 : ℕ)) ^ 2 = 12 ^ 2 * ((10 : ℝ) ^ (18 : ℕ)) ^ 2 := by ring\n336\t    have h2 : ((10 : ℝ) ^ (18 : ℕ)) ^ 2 = (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ) := by rw [← pow_mul]\n337\t    rw [h1, h2]; norm_num\n338\t  rw [h_sq_eq]\n339\t  -- Step 2: collapse the LHS into (12π·13) / (2304·10^76).\n340\t  have h_LHS_clean :\n341\t      (1 : ℝ) * (12 * Real.pi / (16 * (144 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ))))\n342\t        * (13 / (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ))\n343\t      = (12 * Real.pi * 13) / (2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (76 : ℕ)) := by\n344\t    have h36_ne : (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt h36\n345\t    have h40_ne : (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt h40\n346\t    have h_lhs_to_combined :\n347\t        (1 : ℝ) * (12 * Real.pi / (16 * (144 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ))))\n348\t          * (13 / (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ))\n349\t        = (12 * Real.pi * 13) /\n350\t            ((16 * (144 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ))) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ)) := by\n351\t      field_simp\n352\t    rw [h_lhs_to_combined]\n353\t    have h_denom_eq :\n354\t        (16 * (144 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ))) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ)\n355\t          = 2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (76 : ℕ) := by\n356\t      rw [show (16 * (144 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ))) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ)\n357\t            = 2304 * ((10 : ℝ) ^ (36 : ℕ) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ)) from by ring,\n358\t          h_combine]\n359\t    rw [h_denom_eq]\n360\t  rw [h_LHS_clean]\n361\t  -- Step 3: cross-multiply via div_lt_div_iff₀.\n362\t  have h_denom_pos : (0 : ℝ) < 2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (76 : ℕ) := by positivity\n363\t  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ h_denom_pos h31]\n364\t  -- Goal: 12·π·13 · 10^31 < 1 · (2304 · 10^76)\n365\t  -- 156π < 156·3.15 = 491.4 < 2304 ≤ 2304·10^45 = 2304·10^76 / 10^31, so the\n366\t  -- inequality holds.  Prove via h_pi13_bound + the 10^45 ≥ 1 expansion.\n367\t  rw [h_split]\n368\t  -- Goal: 12·π·13 · 10^31 < 1 · (2304 · (10^31 · 10^45))\n369\t  have h_pi13_bound : 12 * Real.pi * 13 < 491.4 := by nlinarith [hpi_lt, hpi_pos]\n370\t  have h_45_ge_one : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ) := by\n371\t    have h0 : (1 : ℝ) = (10 : ℝ) ^ (0 : ℕ) := by norm_num\n372\t    rw [h0]\n373\t    exact pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) ≤ 10) (by decide : (0 : ℕ) ≤ 45)\n374\t  have h_491_lt_2304_10_45 : (491.4 : ℝ) < 2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ) := by\n375\t    have h_2304_le : (2304 : ℝ) ≤ 2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ) := by\n376\t      calc (2304 : ℝ) = 2304 * 1 := by ring\n377\t        _ ≤ 2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ) :=\n378\t            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h_45_ge_one (by norm_num)\n379\t    linarith\n380\t  -- Final assembly: multiply h_491_lt_2304_10_45 by 10^31 (positive), chain.\n381\t  have h_pi13_step : 12 * Real.pi * 13 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) <\n382\t      491.4 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) :=\n383\t    mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_pi13_bound h31\n384\t  have h_491_step : (491.4 : ℝ) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) <\n385\t      (2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ)) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) :=\n386\t    mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_491_lt_2304_10_45 h31\n387\t  have h_RHS_eq : (1 : ℝ) * (2304 * ((10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ)))\n388\t                  = (2304 * (10 : ℝ) ^ (45 : ℕ)) * (10 : ℝ) ^ (31 : ℕ) := by ring\n389\t  rw [h_RHS_eq]\n390\t  linarith\n391\t\n392\t/-- **Cross-channel chained bound (Hughes-Drever follows from\n393\tKostelecky).**  Any prediction satisfying the Kostelecky cosmic-axial-\n394\ttorsion bound automatically satisfies the (looser) Hughes-Drever\n395\trotational-axial-torsion bound — purely by the published-bound\n396\tordering `Kostelecky < Hughes-Drever` (theorem\n397\t`torsionBoundKostelecky_lt_hughesDrever`).  Substantive cross-channel\n398\tcompositional theorem: the Wave 6 main correctness-push directly\n399\timplies passage of the second channel without re-invoking the\n400\tquantitative computation. -/\n401\ttheorem below_kostelecky_implies_below_hughes_drever\n402\t    {x : ℝ} (h : x < torsionBoundKostelecky) :\n403\t    x < torsionBoundHughesDrever := by\n404\t  exact lt_trans h torsionBoundKostelecky_lt_hughesDrever\n405\t\n406\t/-! ## §6. Tracked-Prop bundle for the EC extension -/\n407\t\n408\t/-- **Bundled predicate for the Einstein-Cartan extension.**  An\n409\t`(Λ_UV, N_f, α_EC)` triple \"satisfies the EC extension at the\n410\tcosmological background\" iff:\n411\t\n412\t  1. The EC match residual `δT := torsionAmplitude(α_EC) − torsionAmplitude(1)`\n413\t     vanishes (Wave 6 §3 calibration channel — `α_EC = 1`);\n414\t  2. The torsion amplitude at the cosmological background is strictly\n415\t     positive (Wave 6 §2 — non-vanishing-prediction signature);\n416\t  3. The torsion amplitude at the cosmological background sits below\n417\t     the Kostelecky bound (Wave 6 §5 correctness-push observational-\n418\t     passage condition).\n419\t\n420\tEach conjunct invokes a *distinct* substantive theorem with distinct\n421\talgebraic/numerical content; not P2 redundancy.  Each conjunct\n422\tgenuinely separates \"Wave 6 EC extension at the calibrated point\"\n423\tfrom a distinct failure mode (off-calibration α_EC, vanishing\n424\tprediction, or observational-bound violation). -/\n425\tdef H_EinsteinCartanExtensionHolds (Λ_UV N_f α_EC : ℝ) : Prop :=\n426\t  ecResidual Λ_UV N_f α_EC cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3 = 0 ∧\n427\t  0 < torsionAtCosmologicalBackground Λ_UV N_f α_EC ∧\n428\t  torsionAtCosmologicalBackground Λ_UV N_f α_EC < torsionBoundKostelecky\n429\t\n430\t/-- **Dirac-bundle witness at the Sakharov-Adler calibration and\n431\tnatural microscopic params.**  At `(Λ_UV, N_f, α_EC) = (planckMassGeV,\n432\t16, 1)`, the EC-extension bundle holds.\n433\t\n434\tSubstantive cross-bridges: each conjunct invokes a *distinct*\n435\tsubstantive theorem by name — `ecResidual_at_alpha_one` (Wave 6 §3),\n436\t`torsionAtCosmologicalBackground_pos_at_natural_params` (Wave 6 §2),\n437\tand `torsionAtCosmologicalBackground_at_planck_natural_below_kostelecky`\n438\t(Wave 6 §5 correctness-push).  Not P2 redundancy; the conjuncts probe\n439\tthree distinct structural channels. -/\n440\ttheorem dirac_H_EinsteinCartanExtensionHolds_at_alpha_one :\n441\t    H_EinsteinCartanExtensionHolds planckMassGeV 16 1 := by\n442\t  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩\n443\t  · exact ecResidual_at_alpha_one planckMassGeV 16 cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3\n444\t  · exact torsionAtCosmologicalBackground_pos_at_natural_params\n445\t  · exact torsionAtCosmologicalBackground_at_planck_natural_below_kostelecky\n446\t\n447\t/-- **Falsifier-witness for non-calibrated `α_EC`.**  Under positive\n448\t`(Λ_UV, N_f)` and *any* `α_EC ≠ 1`, the EC extension fails —\n449\tspecifically its first conjunct (the EC match residual at the\n450\tcosmological background).\n451\t\n452\tSubstantive scope: rules out the trivial reading \"any `α_EC` satisfies\n453\tthe bundle\"; the predicate genuinely singles out the Sakharov-Adler\n454\tcalibration.  Drift-protection: proof body invokes\n455\t`ecResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity` (Wave 6 §3) by name — and uses\n456\tthat `cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3 ≠ 0` as the load-bearing non-\n457\tvanishing-spin-density hypothesis. -/\n458\ttheorem perturbed_alpha_not_H_EinsteinCartanExtensionHolds\n459\t    {Λ_UV N_f α_EC : ℝ}\n460\t    (hΛ : 0 < Λ_UV) (hN : 0 < N_f) (hα : α_EC ≠ 1) :\n461\t    ¬ H_EinsteinCartanExtensionHolds Λ_UV N_f α_EC := by\n462\t  intro ⟨h_match, _, _⟩\n463\t  -- cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3 = 13/10^40 > 0, so ≠ 0.\n464\t  have h_n_pos : 0 < cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3 := by\n465\t    unfold cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3\n466\t    have : (0 : ℝ) < (10 : ℝ) ^ (40 : ℕ) := pow_pos (by norm_num) _\n467\t    positivity\n468\t  have h_n_ne : cosmologicalSpinDensityGeV3 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt h_n_pos\n469\t  have h_eq := (ecResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity hΛ hN h_n_ne).mp h_match\n470\t  exact hα h_eq\n471\t\n472\tend SKEFTHawking.EinsteinCartanExtension\n473\t\n474\tend\n475\t"}]},"uuid":"103a4918-fd1a-4aa9-a220-bff6addda511","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:39:26.612Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"266d6235-80f3-45a2-b8fc-90db2e2cb084","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

{"parentUuid":"ac684696-53ec-470a-ba02-fdafdb890db3","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"d7b89794-41f0-46fe-9a20-6d198f8f624f","agentId":"a62f3d0be4fa068fc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PAVMXLuG5rFQsuKmKFKWT2","type":"tool_result","content":"9580\t    pulsar_bound_ok = higher_curvature_predicted_in_observational_band(\n9581\t        N_f, HIGHER_CURVATURE_PARAMS['HC_BOUND_PULSAR_C_SQ']\n9582\t    )\n9583\t    diff_inv_ok = diff_invariance_holds_order_by_order(\n9584\t        N_f, R=12.0, R_sq=144.0, Ricci_sq=36.0, Riemann_sq=24.0,\n9585\t    )\n9586\t    return bool(residual_ok and pulsar_bound_ok and diff_inv_ok)\n9587\t\n9588\t\n9589\t# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n9590\t# Phase 6e Wave 5 — Microscopic-to-Macroscopic Coefficient Match\n9591\t# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n9592\t\n9593\tdef lambda_emerg_microscopic(Lambda_UV, N_f):\n9594\t    \"\"\"Microscopic prediction for the emergent cosmological constant.\n9595\t\n9596\t    Integrating the leading Seeley-DeWitt coefficient `a_0(N_f) =\n9597\t    4 N_f / (4π)²` against the Λ_UV⁴ volume-of-momentum factor gives\n9598\t    the heat-kernel-induced cosmological-constant density:\n9599\t\n9600\t        Λ^emerg(Λ_UV, N_f) = a_0(N_f) · Λ_UV⁴ = (N_f/(4π²)) · Λ_UV⁴.\n9601\t\n9602\t    For SM-like `N_f = 16` and natural `Λ_UV ~ M_Pl ≃ 10¹⁹ GeV`,\n9603\t    `Λ^emerg ~ 9 × 10⁷⁵ GeV⁴`, which exceeds the Planck-2018 observed\n9604\t    value `Λ_obs ≃ 2.6 × 10⁻⁴⁷ GeV⁴` by ~10¹²² — i.e. the classical\n9605\t    cosmological-constant problem reproduced in emergent form.\n9606\t\n9607\t    Lean: MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.lambdaEmergMicroscopic\n9608\t    Aristotle: manual\n9609\t    Source: Sakharov, Sov. Phys. Dokl. 12, 1040 (1968);\n9610\t            Vassilevich, Phys. Rep. 388, 279 (2003), Eq. (4.37)\n9611\t\n9612\t    Parameters\n9613\t    ----------\n9614\t    Lambda_UV : float\n9615\t        Microscopic UV cutoff (GeV).\n9616\t    N_f : float\n9617\t        Number of Dirac-fermion species.\n9618\t\n9619\t    Returns\n9620\t    -------\n9621\t    float\n9622\t        Λ^emerg in GeV⁴.\n9623\t    \"\"\"\n9624\t    return seeley_dewitt_a0(N_f) * float(Lambda_UV) ** 4\n9625\t\n9626\t\n9627\tdef cc_problem_ratio(Lambda_UV, N_f):\n9628\t    \"\"\"Ratio Λ^emerg / Λ_obs for the Decision Gate E.4 verdict.\n9629\t\n9630\t    The emergent cosmological constant divided by the observed\n9631\t    Planck-2018 value `Λ_obs ≃ 2.6 × 10⁻⁴⁷ GeV⁴`. Used by\n9632\t    `cc_decision_gate_e4_verdict` to label the natural-parameter\n9633\t    point as `cc_resolved` / `cc_reproduced` / `cc_intermediate`.\n9634\t\n9635\t    Lean: companion of MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.lambdaEmergMicroscopic\n9636\t          (the ratio is implicit in the quantitative theorem\n9637\t          `lambdaEmergMicroscopic_at_planck_natural_far_exceeds_observed`,\n9638\t          which compares Λ^emerg to 10^100 · lambdaObservedGeV4).\n9639\t    Aristotle: manual\n9640\t    Source: Phase 6e Wave 5 paper42b_cc_emergent §3\n9641\t    \"\"\"\n9642\t    from src.core.constants import MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS\n9643\t    return (\n9644\t        lambda_emerg_microscopic(Lambda_UV, N_f)\n9645\t        / MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['LAMBDA_OBSERVED_GEV4']\n9646\t    )\n9647\t\n9648\t\n9649\tdef cc_decision_gate_e4_verdict(Lambda_UV, N_f):\n9650\t    \"\"\"Categorical Decision-Gate E.4 outcome at given microscopic params.\n9651\t\n9652\t    Returns one of three string labels:\n9653\t      - `'cc_resolved'`     : `|log10(Λ^emerg/Λ_obs)| < 1` (within\n9654\t        an order of magnitude of the observed value),\n9655\t      - `'cc_reproduced'`   : `Λ^emerg/Λ_obs > 10⁶⁰` (the classical\n9656\t        CC problem reproduced in emergent form),\n9657\t      - `'cc_intermediate'` : neither resolved nor reproduced, i.e.\n9658\t        the prediction sits in the diagnostic intermediate band.\n9659\t\n9660\t    The natural choice `(Λ_UV, N_f) = (M_Pl, 16)` lands in\n9661\t    `cc_reproduced`; the diagnostic resolution-locus\n9662\t    `Λ_UV ≃ 4.5 × 10⁻¹² GeV` lands in `cc_resolved`. Either outcome\n9663\t    is publishable per Phase 6e roadmap O.5.\n9664\t\n9665\t    Lean: Python-only verdict label dispatcher; the load-bearing\n9666\t          quantitative anchor is the Lean theorem\n9667\t          `lambdaEmergMicroscopic_at_planck_natural_far_exceeds_observed`\n9668\t          (proves ratio > 10^100 at the natural cutoff, which lands\n9669\t          this Python helper in the `cc_reproduced` branch).\n9670\t    Aristotle: manual\n9671\t    Source: Phase 6e Wave 5 paper42b_cc_emergent §4\n9672\t    \"\"\"\n9673\t    import math\n9674\t    from src.core.constants import MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS\n9675\t    ratio = cc_problem_ratio(Lambda_UV, N_f)\n9676\t    if ratio <= 0:\n9677\t        return MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['DG_E4_VERDICT_INTERMEDIATE']\n9678\t    log10_ratio = math.log10(ratio)\n9679\t    if abs(log10_ratio) < MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['CC_RESOLVED_LOG10_BAND']:\n9680\t        return MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['DG_E4_VERDICT_RESOLVED']\n9681\t    if ratio > MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['CC_REPRODUCED_RATIO_FLOOR']:\n9682\t        return MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['DG_E4_VERDICT_REPRODUCED']\n9683\t    return MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['DG_E4_VERDICT_INTERMEDIATE']\n9684\t\n9685\t\n9686\tdef g_n_microscopic(Lambda_UV, N_f, alpha_ADW=1.0):\n9687\t    \"\"\"Microscopic prediction for `G_N^emerg` parameterised by α_ADW.\n9688\t\n9689\t    Combines the Wave 1 heat-kernel result `G_N_sakharov = 12π/(N_f Λ²)`\n9690\t    with the Phase 6a.1 ADW rescaling\n9691\t    `G_N^emerg = α_ADW · G_N_sakharov`. At the Sakharov-Adler\n9692\t    calibration `α_ADW = 1` the two coincide — the substantive Decision\n9693\t    Gate E.2 closure.\n9694\t\n9695\t    Lean: MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.gNMicroscopic + the cross-bridge\n9696\t          theorem MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.gNMicroscopic_at_alpha_one_eq_G_N_emerg\n9697\t          (which invokes LinearizedEFE.G_N_emerg_at_alpha_one and\n9698\t          HeatKernelExpansion.G_N_from_a2_eq_G_N_sakharov by name).\n9699\t    Aristotle: manual\n9700\t    Source: Phase 6a.1 LinearizedEFE.G_N_emerg_at_alpha_one;\n9701\t            Phase 6e Wave 1 G_N_from_a2_eq_G_N_sakharov\n9702\t    \"\"\"\n9703\t    return float(alpha_ADW) * G_N_from_seeley_dewitt(Lambda_UV, N_f)\n9704\t\n9705\t\n9706\tdef higher_curvature_microscopic_stelle(N_f):\n9707\t    \"\"\"Microscopic Stelle-basis higher-curvature triple `(α, β, γ)`.\n9708\t\n9709\t    Wave 2 closed-form coefficients in the Stelle (R², C², 𝒢) basis\n9710\t    (`a_4_density = α R² + β R_μν² + γ R_μνρσ²` after re-decomposition\n9711\t    via Wave 2's ``a4_density_eq_a4_density_in_RC2GB_basis``):\n9712\t\n9713\t        α(N_f) = -N_f / (324 (4π)²)\n9714\t        β(N_f) = -41 N_f / (4320 (4π)²)\n9715\t        γ(N_f) = +17 N_f / (4320 (4π)²)\n9716\t\n9717\t    `γ > 0` carries the chiral-anomaly-positive sign; `α, β < 0`. The\n9718\t    function returns the triple as a `(alpha, beta, gamma)` tuple in\n9719\t    natural units (no Λ_UV dependence — the triple is dimensionless\n9720\t    times `(4π)⁻²`).\n9721\t\n9722\t    Lean: HigherCurvatureStructure.a4_alpha / a4_beta / a4_gamma +\n9723\t          MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.higherCurvature_stelle_sum_eq\n9724\t          (closed-form aggregate -7 N_f / (810 (4π)²)) +\n9725\t          higherCurvature_stelle_sum_negative.\n9726\t    Aristotle: manual\n9727\t    Source: Christensen & Duff, Nucl. Phys. B154, 301 (1979), Eq. (3.7);\n9728\t            Stelle, Gen. Rel. Grav. 9, 353 (1978);\n9729\t            Phase 6e Wave 2 paper40 §3\n9730\t    \"\"\"\n9731\t    import math\n9732\t    inv_4pi_sq = 1.0 / (4.0 * math.pi) ** 2\n9733\t    alpha = -float(N_f) / 324.0 * inv_4pi_sq\n9734\t    beta = -41.0 * float(N_f) / 4320.0 * inv_4pi_sq\n9735\t    gamma = 17.0 * float(N_f) / 4320.0 * inv_4pi_sq\n9736\t    return (alpha, beta, gamma)\n9737\t\n9738\t\n9739\tdef microscopic_macroscopic_match_residual(Lambda_UV, N_f, alpha_ADW):\n9740\t    \"\"\"Cross-wave coefficient-match residual at given microscopic params.\n9741\t\n9742\t    Closed-form algebraic residual measuring whether the heat-kernel\n9743\t    Wave 1 closed form `G_N_from_a2 = 12π/(N_f Λ_UV²)` matches the\n9744\t    Phase 6a.1 emergent form `G_N^emerg = α_ADW · G_N_sakharov` at the\n9745\t    calibration value `α_ADW = 1`. By construction the residual equals\n9746\t\n9747\t        residual = G_N^emerg(Λ_UV, N_f, α_ADW) - G_N_from_a2(Λ_UV, N_f)\n9748\t                 = (α_ADW - 1) · G_N_sakharov(Λ_UV, N_f),\n9749\t\n9750\t    so it is identically zero iff `α_ADW = 1`. This is the Decision\n9751\t    Gate E.2 anchor expressed at the formula level.\n9752\t\n9753\t    Lean: MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.matchResidual,\n9754\t          MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.matchResidual_eq_zero_iff_alpha_unity\n9755\t    Aristotle: manual\n9756\t    Source: Phase 6e Wave 1 paper39 §5; Wave 5 paper42b §3\n9757\t    \"\"\"\n9758\t    return g_n_microscopic(Lambda_UV, N_f, alpha_ADW) - G_N_from_seeley_dewitt(\n9759\t        Lambda_UV, N_f\n9760\t    )\n9761\t\n9762\t\n9763\tdef microscopic_macroscopic_match_holds(Lambda_UV, N_f, alpha_ADW,\n9764\t                                          tolerance=None):\n9765\t    \"\"\"Bundled Wave-5 predicate: does ``H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch`` hold?\n9766\t\n9767\t    Three-conjunct predicate mirroring the Lean tracked-Prop:\n9768\t\n9769\t      1. Microscopic-macroscopic G_N match residual is zero (i.e.\n9770\t         `α_ADW = 1` within tolerance);\n9771\t      2. Λ^emerg(Λ_UV, N_f) is strictly positive (well-defined emergent\n9772\t         CC);\n9773\t      3. Higher-curvature Stelle coefficients consistent with Wave 2\n9774\t         (γ > 0, α + β < 0 — sign signature).\n9775\t\n9776\t    Any α_ADW ≠ 1 violates conjunct 1; any non-positive (Λ_UV, N_f)\n9777\t    violates conjunct 2.\n9778\t\n9779\t    Lean: MicroscopicCoefficientMatch.H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch,\n9780\t          dirac_H_MicroscopicCoefficientMatch_at_alpha_one\n9781\t    Aristotle: manual\n9782\t    Source: Phase 6e Wave 5 paper42b §5\n9783\t    \"\"\"\n9784\t    from src.core.constants import MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS\n9785\t    if tolerance is None:\n9786\t        tolerance = MICRO_MACRO_PARAMS['MATCH_RESIDUAL_TOLERANCE']\n9787\t    match_ok = abs(float(alpha_ADW) - 1.0) < tolerance\n9788\t    lambda_emerg_pos = lambda_emerg_microscopic(Lambda_UV, N_f) > 0.0\n9789\t    alpha, beta, gamma = higher_curvature_microscopic_stelle(N_f)\n9790\t    stelle_signs_ok = (gamma > 0.0) and (alpha + beta < 0.0)\n9791\t    return bool(match_ok and lambda_emerg_pos and stelle_signs_ok)\n9792\t\n9793\t\n9794\t# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n9795\t# Phase 6e Wave 6 — Einstein-Cartan Extension (torsion from spin current)\n9796\t# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n9797\t\n9798\tdef torsion_amplitude_ec(Lambda_UV, N_f, alpha_EC, n_spin):\n9799\t    \"\"\"Microscopic Einstein-Cartan torsion amplitude from spin current.\n9800\t\n9801\t    In Hehl-style Einstein-Cartan theory the algebraic Cartan torsion\n9802\t    equation reads `T^a_{μν} ∝ G_N · S^a_{μν}` where `S` is the\n9803\t    fermion spin current.  At the trace/scalar level — the load-bearing\n9804\t    parametric content of the Wave 6 model — this collapses to the\n9805\t    closed form\n9806\t\n9807\t        |T_EC|(Λ_UV, N_f, α_EC, n_spin)\n9808\t            = G_N^emerg(Λ_UV, N_f, α_EC) · n_spin\n9809\t            = α_EC · 12π/(N_f · Λ_UV²) · n_spin.\n9810\t\n9811\t    At the Sakharov-Adler calibration `α_EC = 1` this matches the\n9812\t    `G_N^emerg(·, ·, 1) · n_spin` reference (cross-bridge to Phase 6a.1\n9813\t    `G_N_emerg_at_alpha_one`).  The cosmological-background-bath\n9814\t    spin density is `n_s ~ T_CMB³ ≃ 1.3×10⁻³⁹ GeV³` (from\n9815\t    EINSTEIN_CARTAN_PARAMS).\n9816\t\n9817\t    Lean: EinsteinCartanExtension.torsionAmplitude\n9818\t    Aristotle: manual\n9819\t    Source: Hehl, Heyde, Kerlick, Nester, Rev. B5, 1 (1973);\n9821\t            Phase 6e Wave 1 paper39 §5; paper43 §3\n9822\t\n9823\t    Parameters\n9824\t    ----------\n9825\t    Lambda_UV : float\n9826\t        Microscopic UV cutoff (GeV).\n9827\t    N_f : float\n9828\t        Number of Dirac-fermion species.\n9829\t    alpha_EC : float\n9830\t        Einstein-Cartan / ADW dimensionless coefficient (= α_ADW; the\n9831\t        Sakharov-Adler calibration is α_EC = 1).\n9832\t    n_spin : float\n9833\t        Background spin density (GeV³).\n9834\t\n9835\t    Returns\n9836\t    -------\n9837\t    float\n9838\t        |T_EC| in GeV — the magnitude of the predicted torsion amplitude.\n9839\t    \"\"\"\n9840\t    return float(alpha_EC) * G_N_from_seeley_dewitt(Lambda_UV, N_f) * float(n_spin)\n9841\t\n9842\t\n9843\tdef torsion_amplitude_at_cosmological_background(Lambda_UV, N_f, alpha_EC=1.0):\n9844\t    \"\"\"Wave 6 torsion amplitude at the cosmological-bath background.\n9845\t\n9846\t    Specialises ``torsion_amplitude_ec`` to the canonical CMB-bath\n9847\t    spin density ``n_s = COSMOLOGICAL_SPIN_DENSITY_GEV3``. The repo's constant for R² per fermion species is −5/2160, which is −5/(12·180), so comparing 5/360 to 5/2160 shows exactly that factor-of-6 discrepancy, and the sign is flipped relative to Vassilevich's +5/360.
